title: `entire disable` does not reach linked worktrees: settings.local.json is per worktree, so a new `git worktree add` comes back enabled

verdict.rationale: The evidence concerns settings refactors (os.Root anchoring, review profiles, IsSetUpAny added for setup flow) and never mentions how `enabled` in settings.local.json behaves across linked worktrees. The per-worktree scope of the local override was a side effect, not a recorded choice.

rulings.text: Ruling on issue #2160 (Feature request: Goose and Qwen Code agent integrations): we don't add agent integrations to the CLI directly. New agents go through the external agent path first, standalone entire-agent-<name> binaries in https://github.com/entireio/external-agents that talk to the CLI over the external agent protocol. Once an integration is well tested and broadly used, we can consider pulling it into the CLI source tree. Closing as not planned for the CLI itself. [source: gtrrz-victor (CONTRIBUTOR), 2026-08-31, https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/2160#issuecomment-5476033646]

evidence.text:
Give every tree Entire writes to a single os.Root anchor

Entire does filesystem I/O in six trees, and until now each read and write
assembled its own absolute path and handed it to os.ReadFile/os.WriteFile.
Containment was therefore a property each call site had to keep honouring
by hand, and several of them carried comments saying so outright:
PluginDataDir "guarantees ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR always points inside the
managed data subtree", investigate.RunDir noted that "an unvalidated id
would be a path-traversal sink" feeding os.RemoveAll.

Each tree now has one package that owns a shared *os.Root over it, and the
names that reach those roots are relative to them:

  .entire                    entiredir
  git common dir             gitdir
  the working tree           worktreedir
  an agent's session store   agent.SessionStore
  per-user config / cache    userdirs.ConfigRoot / CacheRoot
  managed plugin tree        pluginRoot

The roots memoize through one registry, osroot.Shared, replacing three
separate copies of that map. Directory creation goes through
osroot.MkdirAllNoSymlink, which refuses a component that already exists as
a symlink -- os.Root blocks a symlink that escapes a root but follows one
pointing elsewhere inside it, and an escaping one otherwise surfaces as an
opaque errno far from the cause. entire doctor reports the symlinks that
are already there.

Two anchors are worth calling out because they close a real gap rather
than formalising an existing one. agen

inspect: store profiles in project/local settings, user picks where

Profiles were written to clone-local preferences (.git/entire/preferences.json)
— hidden and unshareable. Persist them to .entire/settings.json (shared,
committed) or .entire/settings.local.json (per-developer) instead, and let the
user choose:
- guided setup / --configure / --edit prompt for the destination,
- scripted --configure honors a new --local flag (default: project),
- non-interactive first run writes the project file.

saveReviewProfile / saveReviewProfileConfig now do a raw read-modify-write on
the chosen file (preserving unrelated keys and other profiles) and ensure
.entire/ exists.

settings.Load now merges review_profiles per profile name across project →
clone-prefs → local, so a team can share profiles in the project file while
individuals add or override profiles locally without hiding the shared set
(previously a later layer replaced the whole map).

Improves the output-destination picker wording and adds tests for the
project-vs-local save (no leakage of local-only profiles into the shared file).

worker.report:
`Load` now reads `enabled` from clone preferences, so a clone-wide `false` overrides the committed `settings.json` in every worktree. Only the loading half of the issue's proposal is done. The test passes after the change, but I never ran it against the old code, so I haven't seen it fail.

- **Fix:** `ClonePreferences` has a new `Enabled *bool` field, and `applyClonePreferences` applies it. The order is `settings.json`, then clone preferences, then `settings.local.json`, so the local file still wins.
- **Not done:** `entire disable` and `entire enable` don't write the flag to `.git/entire/preferences.json` yet. Those commands, the "already enabled" check and the `status --detailed` line are outside `./cmd/entire/cli/settings/`, so I left them alone. Until they write the flag, nothing creates it except hand-editing the preferences file.
